q: Levin's notion of 'universal distribution' assigns to each finite string x the probability m(x) = Σ_{p: U(p)=x} 2^{-|p|}. This is a semi-measure (Σ m(x) ≤ 1) because:
opts: Some programs output infinitely many x
Programs can loop indefinitely (not outputting anything), contributing probability mass that doesn't correspond to any output
exp: Σ_x m(x) = P(U halts and outputs x for some x) = P(U halts) ≤ 1 (not necessarily =1 since U may not halt). This is the 'halting probability' Ω. The universal semi-measure m dominates all computable semi-measures, making it the prior of choice for induction.
